To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Internet has come serve as an additional medium for the transmission of martial arts technique, philosophy, and reflection on the current state the art.
YouTube has become a central platform for the transmission of martial arts, and that the use of this platform has become a central part of the learning of martial arts techniques.

YouTube has been a key tool in disseminating Brazilian Jiu Jisu Jiu Jitsu (BJJ) techniques and philosophies and has become an integral part of BJJ practice and communities of practice, both offline and online.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How do Brazilian Jiu Jitsukas use YouTube for the transmission of martial arts skills and techniques?
how YouTube is being used by practitioners to transmit martial arts techniques, philosophies and practices.
how the Internet is changing the ways in which Brazilian Jiu Jiu practitioners learn, share, and reflect on their martial arts practices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
YouTube has become a central tool in Brazilian Jiu Jitu technique acquisition and dissemination.
Brazilian Jiu Jitu has become an increasingly global art form.
the Internet is not a substitute for face-to-face interaction but rather a tool that can be used to enhance and extend offline communities of practice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown how YouTube is being used by practitioners of Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu to transmit techniques, philosophies, and reflections on the current state-of-the-art.
we are in the process of developing a theoretical model for understanding the relationship between communities of practice and virtual communities of practice.
the Internet has come as a tool to help practitioners learn techniques, to help them learn from the masters, and to help them learn to become the master.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Internet has come not to replace but to complement traditional martial arts practice.
the Internet has become an essential tool for learning and teaching Brazilian Jiu Jitu and other martial arts.
we can no longer consider martial arts as a purely physical activity, but rather as one that involves the use of digital media and social networks to learn, teach, and reflect on techniques.
